precision_baseline.policy_from_user: This version is the precision baseline. Restore every previously removed acceleration; keep it when lossless, stop and ask the user when measurably lossy. An error inside the earlier 1% GPU-comparison tolerance is NOT auto-approved.

key_finding_baseline_is_not_bit_reproduc.consequence: Bit identity cannot gate an optimization on this device. A candidate is only called lossless when its deviation stays inside this measured self-repeat band.
key_finding_baseline_is_not_bit_reproduc.implication_for_round124: The five R124 GPU-comparison gates (0.036%-0.26% video, 0.056%-0.26% audio) sit inside this self-repeat band, so they demonstrate absence of gross implementation error, not operator-level bitwise agreement.

what_was_not_done: The AdaLN and QK-norm+RoPE fusions specifically were not measured; the highest-volume pointwise fusion (SwiGLU) was measured and gained nothing, and the post-FA profile shows the step is staging-bound rather than pointwise-bound.
Encoder acceleration was not worked on; the live encoder stage stays at about 65 s against a 2 s target.
The VAE decode was measured but not brought near its 20 s target (about 132 s).
No universal picture or audio quality claim is made; the audio track stays near -75 dBFS in every configuration, so sample-level audio differences are never used as a quality signal.
remaining_bottleneck: With attention fixed, one warm step is dominated by per-block weight staging through the CPU offload, because the 30.8 GiB DiT is replicated on every rank and cannot be resident in 32 GiB. Closing the remaining step-time gap needs a different mechanism (weight pre-packing or a different staging strategy, quantized transfer, or a larger-memory part), not another precision approximation.
next_work: Either attack the weight-staging mechanism (the only untried lever for step time, since precision approximations are now measured out), or accept 18.41 s/step and spend the next round on encoder latency and the A2/A3 comparison.
